name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-17L 'Longwatch'
description:
The KP-17L is a factory-optioned KP-17 variant with a 165mm extended barrel — 51mm longer than the standard — designed for fixed-post security applications where concealment is irrelevant and terminal performance at extended pistol ranges is the primary concern. The barrel extension is non-compensated, relying on the added mass and length to reduce muzzle climb, and the slide is correspondingly longer with a full-length guide rod assembly. The front sight is an adjustable target unit, and the rear sight is a fully adjustable notch — the only KP pistol in the lineup with factory-adjustable sights at the base configuration. Magazine capacity is 17 rounds of 9x19mm Standard. The grip is standard KP-17, unchanged. The pistol ships with a factory-installed thumb rest on the frame that makes one-handed shooting from a fixed position significantly more stable and two-handed shooting from concealment nearly impossible. It is not designed for concealed carry. It is not designed for movement. It is designed for the guard post, the checkpoint booth, the elevated platform where you sit for eight hours hoping nothing happens.

The KP-17L exists because a significant portion of Slagworks' security contract market involves static positions — gate guards, checkpoint operators, floor monitors in industrial facilities — who need a sidearm that can reach threats at distances where a standard-barrel pistol becomes unreliable but who lack the authority, budget, or space for a long gun. The extended barrel adds meaningful velocity to the 9mm round and the adjustable sights allow a trained operator to make deliberate aimed shots at 80-100 meters with acceptable probability of hit. It is the most capable pistol in the KP lineup that a Tier 1 buyer can legally own, and it is entirely useless in a coat pocket.

The 'Longwatch' nickname comes from the security industry term for an eight-hour solo fixed post — the 'long watch' — and the pistol has become so associated with the role that new checkpoint guards sometimes call their shift a 'longwatch' because of the gun rather than the other way around. An operator carrying a KP-17L is communicating that they are not going anywhere. They are here, they are watching, and they can reach you from the door to the far wall and twenty meters into the parking lot beyond.

tactical_use: The KP-17L is a fixed-post sidearm optimized for ranged engagements from a static or semi-static position. The extended barrel's velocity gain and the adjustable sights' precision capability make it effective at ranges where standard pistols become probabilistic. Operators running it from elevated guard posts or checkpoint positions can engage threats at distances that force an attacker to either break cover or accept the engagement at unfavorable terms. The gun is a liability in close quarters — the long barrel's leverage disadvantage and the thumb rest's interference with alternative grips make room-clearing awkward — but a checkpoint guard who is being rushed through their post has already lost the tactical initiative regardless of their weapon.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's industrial zones, the KP-17L hanging on a checkpoint guard's hip is part of the visual language of 'this facility takes security seriously.' The extra barrel length is visible from distance, and most people in the area know what it means. Guards who carry it tend to develop a particular attitude — patient, watchful, with the slightly detached quality of someone who has spent thousands of hours in the same position. The gun shapes the job it serves. You sit still with a Longwatch. You watch. You wait.
known_users: static security personnel at Slagworks facilities
Tier 1 security workers on fixed-site contracts
story_hooks: A Slagworks checkpoint guard used a KP-17L to make a 94-meter shot that stopped an armed vehicle interdiction — the shot was clean, professional, well beyond what any untrained guard should be capable of, and the guard's employment records show she was hired eight months ago with no listed prior experience.

Three KP-17Ls have been recovered from locations nowhere near any security post — a transit platform, a residential rooftop, a drainage access tunnel — all with the same aftermarket trigger work and all with one round fired. The shots haven't been connected to any reported incident.
